title: Profiling-driven inference ladder: operational heuristics and starter settings
content:
Context / goal:
This note collects a set of operational heuristics (the "inference ladder") to map workload-level profiles to a small set of starter settings for batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization. The aim is to produce a lightweight rulebook that product, solutions, and SRE can use to quickly generate a cost/latency baseline for customers and for our cost model spreadsheets (sheet: "PTO-cost-sweep-2026.xlsx").

Why another draft?
We have many optimization docs but they often assume a single axis tuning (e.g., just quantize or just batch). In practice customers run heterogeneous workloads (chat + embeddings + rerank) and their token distribution changes over time. The inference ladder is designed to be a compact mapping from measured workload signals to combined changes with predictable impact knobs.

Summary of profiling signals (inputs to the ladder)
- median request length (tokens) (L_med)
- 95th percentile request length (L_p95)
- request arrival distribution: qps constant vs. spikey (CV of inter-arrival times)
- fraction of requests that are streaming vs. single-shot
- request reuse/shareable prefixes ratio (P_prefix) — how often requests share a cacheable prefix across requests within a rolling window
- SLO target (p95 latency SLO in ms)
- quality sensitivity: high | medium | low (customer-provided or inferred from evals)

Core idea (the ladder)
- Tier 0 (latency-critical): p95 target < 150ms or streaming-majority (>50% streams)
  - Disable large-batch accumulation (max batch size = 1–2).
  - Aggressive prefix caching where available (cache TTL = short, 30–120s) for high P_prefix.
  - Quantization: only fast-path 8-bit dynamic if model validated for <1% quality drift; otherwise FP16.
  - Cost trade: higher per-token cost accepted for latency.

- Tier 1 (balanced latency/cost): p95 target 150–350ms, CV inter-arrival moderate
  - Enable small micro-batching: target batch = 4–8, max latency budget for batching = 40–80ms.
  - Prefix KV cache enabled with generosity (TTL 5–15m) if P_prefix > 0.05.
  - Quantization: 4/8-bit QConfig (per-model suggested config from experiments) for workloads with low quality sensitivity. Use quantization-only for inference path if eval delta < 2% on customer prompts.

- Tier 2 (cost-first, throughput): p95 target > 350ms or background workloads
  - Aggressive batching: target batch 16–64 depending on GPU type and model. Use continuous-batching mode on the runtime.
  - Cache TTLs long (30m–2h) when requests are repetitive; enable cross-request prefix eviction heuristics to manage memory.
  - Mix of quantization: INT8/INT4 where model architecture permits; enable fallback to higher precision on quality regression.

Adaptive switching recommendations (runtime policies)
- SLO-aware quantization gating: start requests at quantized variant; if rolling eval window shows quality delta > threshold, route a fraction (canary %) to higher precision. Canary fraction ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> fallback.
- Latency/cost governors: attach a small controller that monitors p95 latency and cost/unit; if p95 climbs above SLO, temporarily reduce batching target by N steps and/or increase allocation of lower-latency variant (e.g., move traffic to a non-quantized pool).
- Prefix cache rehydration: if cache hit rate for a key drops below 5% over a 10-min window, mark key as low value and use LRU with explicit demotion to free memory for hot keys.

Practical starter settings (by workload archetype)
- Short chat (L_med < 40 tokens, streaming heavy, high quality sensitivity): tier 0 settings. Suggested: max_batch=2, batch_timeout=20ms, cache_ttl=60s, quant_mode=FP16.
- Multi-turn chat (L_med 60–200 tokens, medium quality sensitivity): tier 1. Suggested: target_batch=8, max_batch=12, batch_timeout=50ms, cache_ttl=10m, quant_mode=8-bit-fast (QAT/llm-specific config).
- Document summarization / long generation (L_med > 400 tokens): tier 2 for cost-first customers, but allow hybrid: first-token latency sensitive then throughput. Suggested: target_batch=32, max_batch=64, batch_timeout=120ms, cache_ttl=30m, quant_mode=INT8/INT4 with fallback.
- Embeddings (short, deterministic): batch-heavy by default. Suggested: target_batch=64, max_batch=256, batch_timeout=250ms, quant_mode=INT8 (if validated), cache_ttl=2h for repeated doc embeddings with content-hash keys.

Spreadsheet knobs and cost model wiring
- Map each heuristic to spreadsheet columns: workload, tier, target_batch, max_batch, batch_timeout_ms, cache_ttl_s, quant_mode, estimated_per_token_ns, measured_gpu_efficiency_pct.
- Suggested metric: compute cost per 1k responses at percentiles (p50/p95) for each scenario and add sensitivity columns for +/–10% traffic burst and +/–20% quality constraint.
- Add a column for operational friction: likely changes that require model retrain or can be applied config-only. Quantization that requires QAT = high friction; post-training static quantization = medium.

Experimental validation plan (quick A/B matrix)
1) Small pilot on dedicated pool with synthesized traffic matching customer token distribution. Measure p50/p95 latency, GPU utilization, cost per token, and quality eval (BLEU/embedding cosine/LLM eval prompts).
2) For each candidate quant config run a 2-hour sweep at 1x and 5x QPS and record degradation.
3) Measure prefix cache working set and hit-rate under sliding 30-min window. Record memory footprint per 100k keys.

Unresolved questions / future work
- How aggressively can we enable INT4 on decoder-only models without retraining for customer prompts? Need a matrix by model family.
- Should we expose an "inference ladder" UI in Optimize that recommends a single line config and a toggle for rapid apply? This would be high value for solutions engineering.
- Auto-suggestion for cache keys: can we infer safe prefix boundaries from conversational traces to avoid over-caching user-specific ephemeral tokens?

Quick implementation notes for SRE/Runtime
- Add a runtime flag to enable SLO-aware batching governor and expose the governor's decisions in request tracing (reason code: "slo:batch_reduce" etc.).
- Add small telemetry events for cache key promotions/demotions (sampled at 1/1000 to avoid cardinality explosion).

Appendix: simple example calculation (document summarization case)
- Baseline (FP16, batch=8): p95=420ms, cost_per_1k_responses=$12.4
- Tier 2 (INT8, batch=32): measured p95=520ms (longer due to scheduling), cost_per_1k_responses=$4.2 (–66%)
- Rule: if customer p95 SLO > 500ms and quality tolerance >= 3% delta, recommend Tier 2 with fallback to FP16 canary at 5%.

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally prescriptive; the goal is to reduce time to an actionable recommendation when onboarding a customer. Please flag any unrealistic latency numbers for specific model families (GPT-like vs. encoder-only).
- If approved, I will add the mapping to the main PTO spreadsheet with macro-level cost sensitivity tabs and a tiny UX mock for the console (one-line apply + metrics preview).

End.
